identity.real_world_identity_notes: The 1998 Toyota GT-One, chassis code TS020, was Toyota Team Europe's GT1 entrant at the 1998 24 Hours of Le Mans. Do not merge it with the revised 1999 LMGTP specification or with the single homologation road car; those versions changed the cockpit and/or hardware. The simulator identity is an exact match to this 1998 race-car family, but a particular chassis or livery is not established.

wheel_rim.notes: The full-resolution Goodwood 2007 photograph of the 1998 Le Mans no.29 car shows a conventional D-shaped rim open across the top, with no readout or shift-light elements on the rim itself. The dash-mounted LCD is not rim equipment.

notes: The reviewed exact-scope sources establish forward gears: 6; gearbox construction: sequential; shift actuation: sequential stick; shift pattern: sequential; wheel-rim shape: d shaped; integrated wheel display: no; conventional rim open-top section: yes; wheel shift lights: no.
The reviewed real-car sources do not establish launch technique, running-shift technique or cut and blip behavior; those baseline fields remain unknown.
AMS2 1.6.9.91 behavior and cockpit values were directly observed and are preserved as simulator overrides where the real baseline is unknown.

Shift actuation is disputed and deliberately left as reviewed. The cited Racers technical review has the 1998 car with a manual shift lever only, revised to paddles later; two secondary retrospectives instead describe 1999 as the year a manual lever was added to back up the sequential change, which implies the opposite for 1998. No manufacturer or homologation source settles it, and no period 1998 in-car source has been found. See dailysportscar.ts020-gt-one.2022.

The PMR car list identifies Toyota GT-One as a 1998 GT1 entry. The exact 1998 Toyota technical and photographic sources already used for the curated record establish the manual-lever sequential car and D-shaped open-top wheel with no rim display or shift lights.

claims.basis: The official 24 Hours of Le Mans history identifies the TS020 as a 1998 and 1999 Le Mans car and describes the 1998 entries as GT-One race cars. The period-specific technical review distinguishes the 1998 manual-lever cockpit from the 1999 paddle-shift revision and lists the 1998 car's six-speed Xtrac sequential gearbox.

Both sources identify a six-speed sequential gearbox for the GT-One. The sources call it an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox with hydraulic shift assistance. They do not establish a dog-ring or synchromesh construction, so the broader sequential category is used. The 1998 specification is explicitly described as having a manual shift lever only in the cockpit; the paddle system belongs to the 1999 revision/test conversion. A sequential gearbox operated by the 1998 manual lever establishes one-gear-at-a-time sequential selection. No source reviewed establishes a first-gear gate position. The full-resolution photograph shows a conventional rim with a flattened lower section, so the project's rim taxonomy classifies it as d-shaped rather than gt-formula. The full-resolution photograph shows no display on the rim. The technical review separately identifies a wheel display as an addition for LM802's later paddle-shift test conversion, not the original 1998 race wheel. The full-resolution photograph visibly shows the upper section of the conventional D-shaped rim removed/open. The full-resolution photograph shows no shift-light elements on the rim. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
